hints: The $50\text{ N}$ force pushes downwards and forwards at $20^\circ$ below the horizontal.
Resolve vertically to find the normal reaction: $R = mg + 50\sin 20^\circ$.
Express the limiting friction as $F = \mu R = 0.3(mg + 50\sin 20^\circ)$.
Resolve horizontally in equilibrium: $50\cos 20^\circ = F$, then solve for $m$ using $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium, noting that the pushing force has a downward component:
$$R = mg + 50\sin 20^\circ$$
$$R = 10m + 50\sin 20^\circ \approx 10m + 17.1010\text{ N}$$

Calculate the limiting frictional force opposing forward motion:
$$F = \mu R = 0.3(10m + 50\sin 20^\circ) = 3m + 15\sin 20^\circ$$

Resolve forces horizontally for motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$50\cos 20^\circ - F = 0$$
$$50\cos 20^\circ = 3m + 15\sin 20^\circ$$
$$3m = 50\cos 20^\circ - 15\sin 20^\circ$$
$$3m = 46.9846 - 5.1303 = 41.8543$$

Solve for the mass $m$:
$$m = \frac{41.8543}{3} \approx 13.9514\text{ kg} \approx 14.0\text{ kg}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the vertical equilibrium equation for the block:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies R - mg - 50\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
$$R = mg + 50\sin 20^\circ$$
where $R$ is the normal contact reaction from the floor.

State the friction formula for dynamic/limiting equilibrium:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $\mu = 0.3$ and the expression for $R$:
$$F = 0.3\left(mg + 50\sin 20^\circ\right)$$

State the horizontal equilibrium equation for motion at constant velocity ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies 50\cos 20^\circ - F = 0$$
$$50\cos 20^\circ = 0.3\left(mg + 50\sin 20^\circ\right)$$

Expand and rearrange to isolate the mass $m$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$50\cos 20^\circ = 0.3(10m) + 0.3(50\sin 20^\circ)$$
$$50\cos 20^\circ = 3m + 15\sin 20^\circ$$
$$3m = 50\cos 20^\circ - 15\sin 20^\circ$$

Evaluate the numerical terms:
$$50\cos 20^\circ = 50 \times 0.9396926 = 46.98463\text{ N}$$
$$15\sin 20^\circ = 15 \times 0.3420201 = 5.13030\text{ N}$$
$$3m = 46.98463 - 5.13030 = 41.85433$$
Divide by $3$:
$$m = \frac{41.85433}{3} \approx 13.9514\text{ kg} \approx 14.0\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Sets up $50\cos 20^\circ = 0.3(10m + 50\sin 20^\circ)$ and solves for $m = 14.0\text{ kg}$.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Correctly resolves the $50\text{ N}$ push into horizontal and vertical components.
